# repo_master

<!-- GENERATED by 0_registry/gen-registry.js from 0_registry/projects-repos.json + 9_others/templates/README.md.tpl. DO NOT EDIT: edit the master or the template, then run `node 0_registry/gen-registry.js`. `node 0_registry/repos-sot.js check` fails when this file differs from a fresh render. -->

The index of every repository this account owns. 75 repositories (58 🌐 public, 17 🔒 private) in 8 areas, 25 projects, 45 families and 13 hubs. `0_registry/clone.sh` pulls down whichever ones you want on this machine. This repo is the index, so the registry has no entry pointing at itself.

## One master file, everything rendered

**Edit [`0_registry/projects-repos.json`](0_registry/projects-repos.json) only, then run `node 0_registry/gen-registry.js`.** It is the ONE master source, validated by [`projects-repos.schema.json`](0_registry/projects-repos.schema.json): the whole hierarchy (areas, projects, families, repos, with codes, labels, descriptions, icons, banners, hubs, farm folders, visibility, developer, renames, consumers) AND each public repo's folder tree (`tree`, depth `folders.max_depth`; private repos carry none). Every file below is rendered from it by the one generator `0_registry/gen-registry.js` and never edited by hand. Its hierarchy is AREA -> PROJECT -> (SUB-CATEGORY) -> FAMILY -> REPO with positional codes (area `N`, project `N.M`, family `N.M.F`, repo `N.M.F.R`); a node's hub repo has the code `<node>.0`. A repo's farm folder, hub, developer, URLs and visibility flag are derived from its place in the tree, never stored twice.

`node 0_registry/gen-registry.js` renders all of them. Folder data: `node 0_registry/refresh-folders-tree.js [--missing] [repo...]` fetches each public repo's tree from GitHub INTO `0_registry/projects-repos.json`, then re-renders. Guards: `node 0_registry/repos-sot.js check` (master schema + rules, every rendered file byte-for-byte, links), `9_others/test/test-repos-sot.sh`, `test-repos-tree.sh`, `test-repo-folders-tree.sh`.

## Layout

The committed symlinks sit in one folder per area or project, named `<code>.<Name>` after its node; sub-folders follow the hub chain, plus the Fin split Corporate / Capital-Markets. Each link is `<farm>/<name>` -> `../` per level + name, pointing out to the one clone in `$CLOUD_GIT_BASE` (default `~/cloud-shared-store/git`). A link that dangles is a repo you have not cloned yet: that is the index working. No project code lives here.

| Folder | Code | Node | Hubs | Repos | What |

## Clone depth

`0_registry/clone.sh` clones with `--depth 1 --shallow-submodules` by default: only the latest commit, so a clone is fast and takes little disk. Each repo has exactly ONE clone (in `$CLOUD_GIT_BASE`); the links point at it, so never keep a second full copy next to it.

```
0_registry/clone.sh <name>...                 # shallow, depth 1 (default)
0_registry/clone.sh --full <name>...          # full history (same as CLONE_DEPTH=0)
CLONE_DEPTH=50 0_registry/clone.sh <name>...  # a deeper shallow clone
git -C <clone> fetch --unshallow     # later, turn an existing clone into full history
git -C <clone> submodule update --init --depth 1   # submodules stay shallow too
```

## Hubs

Every repo except this one carries its hub as a git submodule at `0_hub/<hub>` (a hub carries its parent hub); hubs keep symlinks to their members and a `repos.json` subset checked by `node 0_registry/repos-sot.js check-hub-subsets`. Their `clone.sh` is rendered from [`9_others/templates/hub-clone.sh`](9_others/templates/hub-clone.sh) (`node 0_registry/repos-sot.js sync-hub-scripts`). A public repo never gets a private hub.

## Git attributes (`.gitattributes_ours`)

This repo is plain metadata, so it carries no in-tree `.gitattributes`: sync clients such as GitSync (Android) treat any attributes/filters as a premium feature. The rules live in `.gitattributes_ours` (source: `_dotfiles/git/src/gitattributes`) and are applied locally by `9_others/build.sh`, which sets `git config --local core.attributesFile "$PWD/.gitattributes_ours"`. On a fresh clone, run that one command (or `9_others/build.sh`) to get LF normalisation, union-merge logs and binary handling.
